item.title: 334 · Andrew Perry - What $450M Portfolio Manager Learned From Paul Tudor Jones
item.description:
Andrew Perry spent over 35 years at the intersection of institutional macro research and active portfolio management, including five years as a portfolio manager at Tudor Investment Corporation under Paul Tudor Jones. Managing up to $450 million, Andrew developed a disciplined, multi-dimensional framework to understand where global markets are going and how to structure trades with strict risk management.
After entering the financial markets during the 1987 crash, Andrew learned firsthand how market regimes and trader psychology shape long-term survival. Today, through Macro Pillars, he distills decades of experience into a structured 5-pillar approach, combining government policy, nontraditional liquidity, monetary mechanics, technicals, and price execution, to help traders separate market noise from real edges.
In this conversation, Andrew shares the priceless lessons learned from working alongside legendary trader Paul Tudor Jones, why time horizon and adaptability outweigh being right, and how major market dates (like Treasury funding shifts) create key structural turning points.
In this episode, we explore:• What $450M Portfolio Manager Learned From Paul Tudor Jones• Andrew’s entry into markets during the 1987 crash and how it shaped his view of risk• Life inside Tudor Investment Corporation and managing capital at scale• Why winning 55% of the time is enough when risk-reward is properly managed• The 5-part Macro Pillars framework: Policy, Liquidity, Monetary Mechanics, Technicals & Execution• The significance of non-traditional liquidity, Treasury issuance, and key dates• Understanding the Move Index (bond volatility) as a key indicator over the VIX About Andrew Perry:Andrew Perry is an institutional macro portfolio manager with over 35 years of market experience. He previously managed FX risk at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, served as a Portfolio Manager at Tudor Investment Corporation, and held senior trading roles at Nomura. He is the founder of Macro Pillars, a service designed to provide professionals with a rigorous, independent perspective on macro markets and liquidity.

item.title: 333 · Tim Furey - Why Defense, Not Offense, Makes You a Profitable Trader
item.description:
Tim Furey went from surviving the high-intensity floor trading pits of the Chicago Board of Trade to surviving a near-fatal medical emergency, ultimately building TradeView Markets into a global financial brokerage.After getting his start as Merrill Lynch's youngest commodity broker hire in nearly four decades, Tim risked everything to move to Chicago and learn the craft of floor trading. Through grueling pit battles, he learned the ultimate lesson in market survival: mastering defense and managing risk above all else. Years later, while running his firm and raising a family, Tim survived a sudden medical crisis where doctors gave him a 5% chance of living, an experience that further cemented his relentless drive, resilience, and vision as a leader.In this conversation, Tim breaks down his "hungry dogs run faster" mindset, the lost art of pit trading, why defense creates offense in the markets, and how he turned adversity into fuel to build a global financial services brand.
In this episode, we explore:• Lessons learned from legendary mentor Jeff Stoutland ("Hungry dogs run faster")• Becoming Merrill Lynch’s youngest commodity broker hire in nearly 40 years• Survival in the Chicago Board of Trade pits and the concept of the "power of the lean"• Why risk management and learning how to lose are the keys to long-term trading survival• Transitioning from prop trading to launching TradeView Markets• How a near-fatal medical emergency and a 5% chance of survival reshaped his life and mindset
About Tim Furey:Tim Furey is the Founder and CEO of TradeView Markets, a global multi-asset brokerage serving traders worldwide. Beginning his career in Merrill Lynch’s Futures Division, Tim went on to trade on the floors of the Chicago Board of Trade before transitioning to proprietary trading and entrepreneurship. Known for his resilient leadership and commitment to continuous improvement, Tim leads TradeView Markets while actively supporting amateur sports initiatives, including women's rugby in the Cayman Islands.

item.title: 332 · Steve Nison - The Man Who Introduced Candlestick Charting to the West
item.description:
Steve Nison came to Wall Street as a technical analyst in the late 1980s, discovered an obscure Japanese charting methodology, and spent years translating rare texts to introduce candlestick charting to the Western world.Through his landmark research, bestselling books, and institutional training at major firms like Merrill Lynch and Daiwa Securities, Steve opened the eyes of global investors to the power of price action and market psychology. Today, candlestick charts are the universal standard across virtually every financial trading platform in the world.In this conversation, Steve pulls back the curtain on how candlesticks first arrived in the West, sharing the cultural and military roots of candlestick patterns, market psychology, and his foundational Trading Triad framework.
In this episode, we explore:• How Steve Nison introduced Japanese candlestick charting to the Western world• Discovering candlesticks at Merrill Lynch through a Japanese broker and early Bloomberg charts• Translating 13+ rare Japanese books and working with Japanese technical organizationsy• Why candlesticks complement rather than replace traditional Western technical analysis• The mechanics behind his "Trading Triad" approach• Steve’s reflection on how candlesticks became the global charting standard• Advice for the next generation of traders pulling up candlestick charts today
About Steve Nison:Steve Nison, CMT, is the founder and president of Candlecharts.com and is widely regarded as the authority who introduced Japanese candlestick charting to the Western world. He authored the landmark classic Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques, which has been translated into 21 languages and fundamentally changed technical analysis across global financial markets. Over his 30+ year career, Steve has advised top institutional financial firms including Fidelity, J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, NYSE, and NASDAQ market makers and has presented by request at the World Bank and the Federal Reserve. Links +

item.content:encoded:
Steve Nison came to Wall Street as a technical analyst in the late 1980s, discovered an obscure Japanese charting methodology, and spent years translating rare texts to introduce candlestick charting to the Western world.
Through his landmark research, bestselling books, and institutional training at major firms like Merrill Lynch and Daiwa Securities, Steve opened the eyes of global investors to the power of price action and market psychology. Today, candlestick charts are the universal standard across virtually every financial trading platform in the world.
In this conversation, Steve pulls back the curtain on how candlesticks first arrived in the West, sharing the cultural and military roots of candlestick patterns, market psychology, and his foundational Trading Triad framework.

In this episode, we explore:
• How Steve Nison introduced Japanese candlestick charting to the Western world
• Discovering candlesticks at Merrill Lynch through a Japanese broker and early Bloomberg charts
• Translating 13+ rare Japanese books and working with Japanese technical organizationsy
• Why candlesticks complement rather than replace traditional Western technical analysis
• The mechanics behind his "Trading Triad" approach
• Steve’s reflection on how candlesticks became the global charting standard
• Advice for the next generation of traders pulling up candlestick charts today

About Steve Nison:
Steve Nison, CMT, is the founder and president of Candlecharts.com and is widely regarded as the authority who introduced Japanese candlestick charting to the Western world. He authored the landmark classic Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques, which has been translated into 21 languages and fundamentally changed technical analysis across global financial markets. Over his 30+ year career, Steve has advised top institutional financial firms including Fidelity, J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, NYSE, and NASDAQ market makers and has presented by request at the World Bank and the Federal Reserve.  Links +
